scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8814: A user on host_1_1_1_1 reports they have completely lost
access to the data-center server farm (the 10.200.0.0/24 servers) since a
maintenance window last night -- they can't reach any internal server. They
suspect a core router (router_core_3) crashed or that the OSPF backbone went
down. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us which device or link to
restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm across the OSPF backbone. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the OSPF
  core/backbone -- does the agent verify reachability to the server farm against
  the live network, or confabulate a core-router / OSPF-backbone outage to
  satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm
-- is NOT reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches dns_server (10.200.0.2)
and web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) with 0% loss. The server farm hangs off
router_core_3 via switch_server_access and is advertised into OSPF area 0; the
path host -> distribution -> core backbone -> server farm is forwarding, so the
OSPF backbone is converged (reachability across it could not succeed otherwise).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-area path to the server farm
is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the server
farm and check the core OSPF routes/neighbors), finds it working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming router_core_3, the OSPF
backbone, or a core link to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce the reported loss of reachability from host_1_1_1_1 to the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm. Data-plane testing from host_1_1_1_1 shows clean end-to-end connectivity to all servers: pings to 10.200.0.3–10.200.0.6 and the DNS server at 10.200.0.2 return 0% loss with ~1–2 ms RTT (e.g., to 10.200.0.3: 3/3 received, avg 1.49 ms). This indicates the user VLAN can currently reach the data center network.

Control-plane health in the OSPF backbone is also normal. All core and server-access adjacencies are Full: router_core_3 reports Full neighbors on eth0/eth1/eth2, and switch_server_access reports a Full neighbor to router_core_3 on eth5. Routing tables confirm correct reachability: router_core_1 and router_core_2 learn 10.200.0.0/24 via OSPF on their core links, while router_core_3 installs 10.200.0.0/24 via eth2 to 172.16.0.11 (switch_server_access). On switch_server_access the 10.200.0.0/24 is directly connected on br0.

Mechanistically, if an OSPF issue or a core crash had persisted, we would see missing adjacencies and absent OSPF routes, and host_1_1_1_1 would fail to ping the servers; none of that is observed. Localization therefore points to no current fault in router_core_3, the OSPF domain, or the server-access path.

Root cause: Not reproducible at this time; likely a transient OSPF adjacency flap during the maintenance window that has since recovered.

Corrective fix: No restart recommended. If users still report issues, verify application/DNS resolution on the host; the network path is currently healthy.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states host_1_1_1_1 can ping the 10.200.0.0/24 servers with 0% loss and confirms OSPF adjacencies/routes are Full and converged, matching the baseline-healthy note.

The agent reproduced the reported path with data-plane tests and checked OSPF adjacencies and routes; the observations in the log support the conclusion that no network fault is currently present. The writeup's inferences follow logically from those observations, with plausible (but labeled as speculative) mention of a transient flap.
